questions.text: What is the worst case time complexity of inserting [latex]n^2[/latex] elements into an AVL-tree with n elements initially?
questions.solution:
Each AVL insertion costs [latex]O(\log N)[/latex], where N is the current size, at most [latex]n^2+n[/latex]. [latex]\log(n^2+n)=\Theta(\log n)[/latex].

[latex]n^2[/latex] insertions [latex]\times[/latex] [latex]\Theta(\log n)[/latex] = [latex]\Theta(n^2\log n)[/latex]

Answer: [latex]\Theta(n^2\log n)[/latex]

questions.text: The preorder traversal of a binary search tree is 15,10,12,11,20,18,16,19. Which one of the following is the postorder traversal of the tree?
questions.solution:
Build the BST from the preorder (root first):
- Root 15; left subtree {10, 12, 11}: 10 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] right 12 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] left 11.
- Right subtree {20, 18, 16, 19}: 20 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] left 18 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] children 16 and 19.

Postorder (left, right, root): 11, 12, 10, 16, 19, 18, 20, 15

Answer: 11, 12, 10, 16, 19, 18, 20, 15

questions.text: Let T be a full binary tree with 8 leaves. (A full binary tree has every level full.) Suppose two leaves a and b of T are chosen uniformly and independently at random. The expected value of the distance between a and b in T (i.e., the number of edges in the unique path between a and b) is (rounded off to 2 decimal places) ___________ .
questions.solution:
8 leaves, height 3. Fix leaf a; b is uniform over the 8 leaves (b can equal a):
- same leaf: distance 0 (1 leaf)
- sibling: distance 2 (1 leaf)
- same subtree of height 2: distance 4 (2 leaves)
- other half: distance 6 (4 leaves)

[latex]E=\frac{0+2+2\times4+4\times6}{8}=\frac{34}{8}=4.25[/latex]

Answer: 4.25

questions.text:
Consider the following statements:

I. The smallest element in a max-heap is always at a leaf node.
II. The second largest element in a max-heap is always a child of the root node.
III. A max-heap can be constructed from a binary search tree in [latex]\Theta (n)[/latex] time.
IV. A binary search tree can be constructed from a max-heap in [latex]\Theta (n)[/latex] time.

Which of the above statements is/are TRUE?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- I: a node with a child is larger than that child, so the minimum has no child [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] it is a leaf [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.
- II: the 2nd largest can only be smaller than the root, so its parent must be the root [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.
- III: build-heap on any array (e.g. the BST's elements) takes [latex]\Theta(n)[/latex] [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.
- IV: a BST from a heap in [latex]\Theta(n)[/latex] would give an [latex]O(n)[/latex] comparison sort (inorder traversal) [latex]\text{---}[/latex] FALSE.

Answer: I, II and III

questions.text: Which traversals of Tree-1 and Tree-2, respectively, will produce the same sequence?
questions.solution:
Traversals from the figure:
- Tree-1 postorder: G J I H E F D B C A
- Tree-2 inorder: G J I H E F B D C A; preorder: G F E I J H C D B A

Tree-1 postorder and Tree-2 inorder are close but differ (D B vs B D), and the other pairs differ from the start. No option gives the same sequence.

Answer: None of these
